task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-07-13, in the area of structural roles and influence):
Lineup coverage (>=1 organizer, shaper, terminal) varies within team, is separable from talent/counts, and talent control behaves.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 420,993 possessions; 90 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

historical_evidence.finding: Adaptation quality (pct_ran_BEST - pct_ran_AVOID) failed to predict series wins after controlling for RS net-rating talent; corr(talent,adapt)=+0.124, logistic adapt p=0.275; n~55 series cannot separate coaching adaptation from roster quality.
Series-level AVOID share vs winning confounded by team quality; rho=-0.26 p=0.07 with n=50 series underpowered; game-level rho inflated by n and team-quality confound.
Persistent Impact Score gate failed: DRIVE lift flat and collapsed under within-team baseline, revealing team-quality confound; callable play-type horizons = 0.
Exploratory superstar suppression: Jokic vs MIN lineup PPP 0.814 (n=59); no placebo or matching; later sequence work treated similar star-chain gaps as artifacts.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Adaptation quality vs talent logistic regression
failed_approaches.why: Talent confound; after controlling talent adapt p=0.275; n~55 series insufficient power.
Team-quality confound; series n=50 underpowered to separate from overall quality.
Apparent effects were artifacts of team-quality confound; within-team baseline eliminated them.

evidence_establishes: Talent confounding is pervasive in possession-level derived-player-label analyses and routinely produces spurious signals.
Without strong within-team controls or player fixed effects, effects attributed to role-based variables collapse to team quality.
Sample sizes at the series or team level (50-100 units) are inadequate to separate role effects from talent; possession-level designs can achieve large N but must address within-team variation.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether lineup coverage of organizer[path] varies meaningfully within team.
That such coverage has any causal effect on PPP independent of the individual players' talent.
The stability and reliability of structural role labels across seasons and when applied to lineups.
Power or effect size estimates for the proposed lineup-coverage analysis.
own_inferences: Within-team fixed effects (player or lineup) can partly mitigate team-level confound but do not eliminate within-team talent differences between lineups with and without coverage.
Structural roles are derived from play-type initiations and usage; if defined from the same season as the test, they risk outcome-derived label bias and look-ahead leakage.
A viable design must assign roles from prior seasons only, and employ placebo shuffles of role labels to test for spurious coverage effects.
Exposure sparsity may be problematic if most lineups for a given team have full coverage, leaving little within-team variation.
uncertainties: The within-team variation in coverage (≥1 organizer, shaper, terminal) is unknown; some teams may rarely field lineups missing one role.
Role assignments may shift across seasons due to player ageing, role changes, or trades, reducing reliability of prior-season labels.
The minimum effect size of interest is not specified; even if detectable, practical significance may be small.

historical_effect.explanation: Retrieved evidence shows that superficially similar tests (adaptation vs talent, AVOID share vs winning) collapsed under talent confound and insufficient power. This warns that a naive regression of lineup PPP on coverage would likely be confounded. The decision is therefore to proceed only with a design that uses prior-season role labels, player fixed effects, and placebo falsification to guard against the historical failure modes.

blocking_constraints.text: If structural roles are computed from the same season's data as the outcome, future information leaks into the coverage indicator, creating an artifact.
If the vast majority of a team's possessions occur with full coverage, within-team variation will be too low to estimate the coverage effect precisely.
Even with player fixed effects, lineup coverage may proxy for synergy or unmeasured talent that is not captured by individual player statistics.

prior_work.summary: No earlier study directly tested lineup coverage of organizer, shaper, and terminal roles. Indirect evidence highlights talent confounding and sample-size risks in role-based possession analyses.

risks.text: Lineups with full coverage likely include more talented players; player fixed effects may not fully account for lineup-specific synergies.
If roles are defined using play-type and usage data from the same games as the outcome PPP, the coverage indicator is circular.
Role assignment must avoid future information; cross-season or pre-registered cut-off is essential.
Structural role classification near the usage median is noisy; misclassification can attenuate or inflate effects.
Within-team variation in coverage may be limited if coaches rarely play lineups missing one of the three role types.
Coverage definitions based on high-usage roles may coincide with hot shooting streaks, leading to regression-to-the-mean bias.
Testing many role combinations or splitting by play type inflates false positives unless multiplicity is pre-registered and corrected.

design.estimand: The within-team causal effect of a lineup having at least one organizer, at least one shaper, and at least one terminal (coverage=1) versus missing at least one of those roles (coverage=0) on possession-level points per possession (PPP), controlling for player identities, game state, and opponent strength.
design.unit: possession (or 10-player stint if structural roles are defined at stint level)
design.sample: All non-garbage-time possessions from NBA 2025-26 regular season (data from 2025-26 regular season file, excluding final 2 minutes of quarters when margin >20). Teams with fewer than 100 uncovered possessions (coverage=0) are excluded to ensure within-team variation.
design.power: With ~400,000 possessions and an expected covered/uncovered ratio of at least 5:1, a difference of 0.02 PPP (Cohen's d ~0.08) would be detectable at 80% power with alpha=0.01, provided at least 15 teams have adequate variation.
design.controls: Player fixed effects (dummies for each of the ten players on court) to absorb individual offensive/defensive talent; game period (1Q-4Q); score margin (categorical: tied, lead ≤5, lead 6-10, lead >10); home/away; opponent defensive rating (rolling 10-game).
design.falsification: 1) Shuffle role labels among players within each team while preserving per-team counts; re-estimate coverage effect – must vanish. 2) Use random cutoffs for usage and residual influence instead of the published thresholds – effect should disappear. 3) Restrict to games where all three role players are available but the lineup still varies coverage (e.g., due to resting) to isolate coverage from injury selection.
design.multiplicity: Primary test: coverage (binary) on PPP in a linear mixed model with player random effects (or player FEs). Pre-register one tail test (positive). If subgroup analyses by play type are run, apply Bonferroni correction (k ~8 play types).
design.decision_rule: Reject null of no coverage effect if p<0.01 (one-sided) and all three placebo tests yield p>0.1. If any placebo fails, treat as artifact/inconclusive. If primary p>0.01, declare null not rejected.
design.data_version: NBA 2025-26 regular season through 2026-04-13; structural roles assigned from 2024-25 regular season and 2025 playoffs (last completed season before the test period).
